educationalModelNote: All numerical models are simplified educational models, not specifications of a real robot.

missions.title: SENSE THE BODY
missions.concept: Proprioceptive sensors measure different physical effects; no single sensor directly provides complete body state.
missions.scenario: The robot is leaning with biased inertial data. Compare sensing strategies rather than editing the sensor error.
missions.goalText: Choose a sensing strategy that builds usable state from complementary evidence.
missions.transferText: Do not pretend the uncertain foot is perfect; keep multiple evidence sources in the estimate.

missions.title: TIMING & CALIBRATION
missions.concept: A precise measurement can still be wrong for control if its frame, calibration or timestamp is wrong.
missions.scenario: Head motion rate is imposed. Tune pipeline latency and clock calibration.
missions.goalText: Keep the observation temporally aligned enough for the moving head.
missions.transferText: Tighten timing when the same error becomes more damaging at higher motion rate.

missions.title: FUSE SENSORS
missions.concept: Sensor fusion should weight information by uncertainty and failure mode, not by whichever sensor has the largest nominal resolution.
missions.scenario: The IMU and vision errors are measured evidence. You choose only how much trust to allocate.
missions.goalText: Choose a fusion weight that reduces the combined estimate error.
missions.transferText: Shift trust after the visual cue becomes unreliable; you cannot edit the observed error.

missions.title: STATE ESTIMATION
missions.concept: An estimator predicts state, compares measurements with predictions and carries uncertainty; wrong contact assumptions can create confident drift.
missions.scenario: Foot slip is imposed by reality. Tune process and measurement uncertainty instead of editing the slip.
missions.goalText: Keep estimate bias and uncertainty bounded.
missions.transferText: Stop over-trusting the false stationary-contact assumption.

missions.title: PERCEPTION UNDER UNCERTAINTY
missions.concept: Planning should consume uncertainty, sensor age and confidence; when perception degrades, safe behavior often means slowing or increasing clearance.
missions.scenario: Localization uncertainty is measured evidence. Choose speed and planned clearance.
missions.goalText: Preserve clearance after accounting for speed and measured uncertainty.
missions.transferText: Adapt speed or clearance when uncertainty expands.

missions.title: PERCEPTION GATE
missions.concept: Integrate sensor timing, state uncertainty and degraded perception into decisions that remain safe.
missions.scenario: Each gate case imposes sensor age and uncertainty. You control motion and clearance, not sensor quality.
missions.goalText: Complete the three perception gate cases.

gateCases.name: TIMING
gateCases.text: With nominal uncertainty, keep motion error below 3 cm at useful speed.

gateCases.name: UNCERTAINTY
gateCases.text: With larger uncertainty, keep clearance above the full buffer by 8 cm.

gateCases.name: DEGRADED MODE
gateCases.text: With stale, uncertain state, slow and enlarge clearance enough to preserve 10 cm margin.
